subject.title: [Analysis] Identify performance bottlenecks in native OpenClaw setup on constrained VPS

question: What measurement environment and acceptance criteria should count as sufficient for this native-Linux VPS reasoning-latency analysis?
rationale: The remaining work is a broad investigation and runbook/product scope choice rather than a single source-level defect that automation can safely infer from current code.

options.title: Scope a runbook first
options.body: Publish a focused native-Linux VPS performance runbook that names required traces, commands, metrics, estimated layer costs, and follow-up issue split criteria.

options.title: Require real reporter-like trace first
options.body: Keep the issue open but wait for a CPX32-class trace or maintainer-provided run before writing documentation or adding spans.

options.title: Split into narrow instrumentation issues
options.body: Close this as too broad only after maintainers create canonical follow-up issues for each missing span or optimization area.

recommendation.title: Scope a runbook first
recommendation.body: Publish a focused native-Linux VPS performance runbook that names required traces, commands, metrics, estimated layer costs, and follow-up issue split criteria.

likelyOwner.reason: The current source and docs history for the central diagnostics/context/Linux-host surfaces routes primarily through steipete.
